Customer churn ≠ revenue churn

Opening paying cohort, attributed to opening plan

Customer churn counts customers ending at $0. Revenue churn weights their lost MRR. Downgrades are contraction, excluded from both churn rates.

Three measures, three different questions

Recurring revenue

Month-end contracted run rate, net of recurring discounts.

Invoiced charges

Daily prorated service charges, billed in arrears.

Collected cash

Payments received this month, including prior invoices.

Invoiced charges are not GAAP recognized revenue. Payment failure alone leaves MRR unchanged until service cancellation.

Acquisition quality matters more than signup volume.

Descriptive association, not a causal effect. Generator intentionally links activation to retention. Reactivated customers count as retained at each horizon; this is point-in-time retention, not survival.

Which channels bring customers who stay?

90 days after landmark · full eligible history

95% Wilson intervals summarize sampling uncertainty within this generated population. They do not capture model or real-world uncertainty.

Censoring and fair comparisons

Each horizon includes only customers observed long enough and paying at day 30. Cohort composition therefore changes with the horizon. Channels also differ in plan, activation, and signup mix; rankings are descriptive and do not justify causal budget reallocations.

A transparent counterfactual

What if fewer customers left?

One-month MRR sensitivity using the selected month's observed opening-cohort losses.

These sliders reduce lost recurring revenue, not the number of failed invoices. They assume rescued customers stay on their opening plan through month-end; no extra acquisition, expansion, cost, or cash collection is assumed.

SCENARIO CLOSING MRR

Range varies each effectiveness assumption by the selected uncertainty, clipped to 0–100%. It is a sensitivity bound, not a confidence interval or forecast. Effects are additive across disjoint exit reasons.

Metric contract

GRR = (opening − contraction − churn) / opening.

NRR = (opening + expansion − contraction − churn) / opening.

Expansion is the net positive MRR change among opening payers who still pay at month-end; includes discount expiry.

New is the first positive month-end MRR. Reactivation requires an earlier positive month-end. Customers who enter and leave within a month are visible in events and invoices, but not endpoint MRR movements.

Scope & limitations

24 months · January 2024–December 2025 · USD · seed 7142025. One concurrent subscription per customer; each reactivation opens a new spell. Event plan is authoritative; subscription plan records the spell's starting plan.

All data is fabricated. Channel quality, activation association, and 2025 deterioration are encoded assumptions. No taxes, refunds, annual prepayments, currency changes, or accounting revenue recognition. December cash is censored at year-end; open invoices are not payment failures.

REVENUE LAB / A SYNTHETIC ANALYTICS CASE STUDYMethods demonstrate analysis. Findings do not establish real customer behavior.
